subject: biology-1
question: During the elongation phase of translation, a **tRNA** molecule carrying an **anticodon** docks at the ribosome. Which statement best describes what this tRNA does?

options.text: It brings its amino acid to the ribosome and pairs its anticodon with the mRNA codon
It unwinds the DNA so RNA polymerase can read the template strand
It carries the mRNA out of the nucleus and into the cytoplasm
It cuts introns out of the pre-mRNA during splicing

explanation: Each tRNA carries one specific amino acid, and its anticodon base-pairs with the complementary codon on the mRNA, delivering the right building block at each step of elongation. B describes the job of helicase and RNA polymerase during transcription. C describes mRNA export, and D describes splicing, both done by other molecules.
